clue.text: Setter, this setter, to pause — he needs rest following Beelzebub

definitions.note: adjectival: in the manner of the devil, like a devotee of Satan

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself is ME
Phi is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter
to pause is to stop
to rest against something is to lean on it

explanation.surface: The setter calls for a break: he needs a rest after struggling with a demon of a clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter names himself twice: ME and his pseudonym PHI, with ME first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the devil of the Faust legend, so the adjective describes devilish, Satan-like behaviour.

clue.text: Hardy hero, reduced fellow, receiving money for opinion

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the name goes

parts.note: Jude the Obscure is the title hero of Thomas Hardy's novel

indicators.note: receiving means the word for fellow takes the money letter inside it

parts.note: a fellow is a gent

explanation.surface: A literary hero, cut down to size, is bribed into giving his view.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy wrote Jude the Obscure; 'reduced' trims JUDE to JUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A considered view or assessment can be called a judgment, as in 'in my judgment'.

clue.text: Metal shard I placed higher up

indicators.note: in a down entry, higher up means earlier, so the letter I is moved towards the start

parts.note: a shard is a sliver of glass or wood

explanation.surface: Someone describes putting a sharp piece of metal up on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed higher up' moves the I in SLIVER one place earlier, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element, symbol Ag.

clue.text: Distant energy sources to the fore for US investment company

indicators.note: to the fore puts the sources word at the front of the charade

parts.note: wells are sources of water or oil
distant means far
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Remote power sources taking the lead for an American investment firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells Fargo is a large American bank and financial services firm, once famous for stagecoaches.

clue.text: Stars turning up in ordinary locations

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the stars are tucked inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Stars appearing in everyday places.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden letters: 'in' signals them. In a down entry 'turning up' reads ARYL from ordinARY Locations backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyra is a constellation, a named group of stars in the northern sky.

clue.text: Describing most of the dictionary in spite of everything

definitions.meaning: nearly every headword is listed alphabetically later than the little word 'all'
an idiom meaning nevertheless, when all is said and done

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry that holds good despite everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday idiom for 'nevertheless', and literally describes words placed later in the alphabet than 'all'.

clue.text: Detest first couple of lowbrow articles

indicators.note: first couple of takes just the opening two letters of the word lowbrow

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the opening pair of trashy newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' is grammar, not journalism: the two English articles.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to hate it intensely, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Decadent period: ingenuity has ten kinks

indicators.note: kinks are twists, so the letters of the phrase are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: An era of decadence has ten kinks to its ingenuity.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1890s in Britain are remembered as a decade of aestheticism and moral laxity, hence the nickname.

clue.text: English abruptly claiming it, showing a degree of culture

indicators.note: claiming means taking the word it inside

parts.note: abruptly, as in brusquely, means rudely

explanation.surface: An Englishman curtly lays claim to something, revealing a cultured background.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is learning, so acting in a learned, scholarly way shows cultivation.

clue.text: Footballing group crushing my plants

indicators.note: crushing means squeezing the exclamation inside the football body

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association
'Lor!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'

explanation.surface: A football team trampling the plants, to someone's dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the collective term for the plant life of a region.

clue.text: Have light go off? Then this may not be present!

definitions.text: Then this may not be present!
definitions.note: if the lights fail, the electrical power supply may be missing

indicators.note: off means spoilt or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: If your light goes off, there may be no electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like the light switching off but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights going out suggests a power cut, when the strong electrical current is absent.

clue.text: Endless staying-power reflected in boat

indicators.note: reflected means the word is read backwards, as in a mirror
endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: guts means courage and staying-power

explanation.surface: A boat shows endurance, mirrored in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a small powerful boat that tows larger vessels.

clue.text: Son to pick up clipping

definitions.note: a gerund for the act; a shear is a single clipping of a sheep's fleece

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: A son goes to collect some cuttings.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearing is a cut of the fleece, so the noun sense matches a single trim.

clue.text: Heaven beginning to tremble after decisive end of prayer

indicators.note: after puts the tremble letter behind the other pieces

parts.note: firm means resolute, decisive
Amen is said at the end of a prayer

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of tremble

explanation.surface: Heaven begins to shake after a resolute end to the prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the sky, the heavens in poetic and biblical language.

clue.text: Sport unexciting after Ed departs, as one sees with rock-climbing?

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: departs means the name Ed leaves the word

parts.note: pedestrian means dull and unexciting

explanation.surface: Ed has left, and the sport seems dull; perhaps rock-climbing would liven things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupestrian means living on or among rocks, or inscribed on rock, as a climber's surroundings are.

clue.text: Military commander to be given leadership of regiment in just over four weeks

parts.note: OC is Officer Commanding

indicators.note: leadership of takes the first letter of regiment

explanation.surface: An officer is to be given command of a regiment within a month.
explanation.definitionFit: This month has 31 days, a little over four weeks.

clue.text: Most of literary family is seen around very significant peak

indicators.note: seen around means the letters surround the very abbreviation
most of drops the final letter

parts.note: the Bennets are the family of Pride and Prejudice

explanation.surface: Most of a famous fictional family is spotted near a great mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The literary family is Jane Austen's Bennets, of Pride and Prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Nevis in Scotland is the highest mountain in the British Isles.

clue.text: Car's attraction? Principal one overlooked

parts.note: pull means attraction or influence

indicators.note: overlooked means the digit-like letter for one is missed out

parts.note: principal means main
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: What makes a car appealing? Its main feature has been ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pullman is a luxurious railway carriage, a railway car.

clue.text: Biblical character: "I am upset about men serving over Christmas period?"

indicators.note: about means wrapped around the other letters
upset in a down clue turns the words over, reading them backwards

parts.note: the two words are taken as letters

indicators.note: over in a down entry puts one piece above the next

parts.note: OR is other ranks, serving soldiers
Dec is December

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being upset that soldiers are working over Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Esther, Mordecai is Esther's cousin who foils Haman's plot.

clue.text: Hung over, embracing second American to a large extent

definitions.note: adjective needed; read as 'large to a great degree', i.e. enormous

indicators.note: embracing means holding the short-time word inside

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
O is an over in cricket scoring
US means American

explanation.surface: A hungover American, hugged at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hung over' looks like one hangover word; it splits into HUNG and O, an over in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Humongous is informal American slang for enormous, very large indeed.

clue.text: Calling one to probe measuring device

indicators.note: to probe means to go inside the measuring device word

parts.note: a meter is a measuring device
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vocation for someone who probes gauges.
explanation.definitionFit: A métier is a person's trade or vocation, their calling in life.

clue.text: Strange feeling about capital of Italy — it's an Italian city

indicators.note: about means the turn wraps round the capital letter

parts.note: a turn is a sudden spell of feeling odd or ill

indicators.note: capital of takes the first letter of Italy

explanation.surface: A weird feeling about the capital of Italy, which is a different city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of Italy' tempts with ROME; it only gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin, in Piedmont, is a major city of northern Italy.

clue.text: Gun, shot in extremity, giving voice

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the extremity word

parts.note: a toe is at the extremity of the body

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shot in the foot cries out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language or voice, as in hounds that 'give tongue'.

clue.text: Biblical refugee's fate

definitions.meaning: one's portion or destiny in life

explanation.surface: What became of a refugee in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Lot fled the destruction of Sodom; separately, one's lot is one's destiny.

clue.text: Very athletic blokes brought into part of hospital area

indicators.note: brought into means placed inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat
ironmen compete in gruelling triathlons

explanation.surface: Super-fit men are admitted to a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: An environment is a surrounding area or setting.

clue.text: Very long time looking heavenward — to see me in 5?

indicators.note: in a down entry looking upward means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: After a long wait gazing at the sky, a star invites you to spot it in a constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 refers to 5 Down, the constellation LYRA, of which this is the brightest star.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: One looking to oust leader, one from Asian republic

indicators.note: to oust leader removes the first letter

parts.note: a gazer is one who looks
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone seeking to topple a leader, from a republic in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Azeri describes people or things of Azerbaijan, a former Soviet republic.

clue.text: Good litre in a tea-urn, needing stirring — like some sugar?

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A litre in the urn needs stirring, as you might stir in sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Granulated sugar is in small grains, so the adjective describes such sugar.
